subject: Finalizing custody redundancy exhibit & SLA carveouts
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novushealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@novushealth.com, ciso@novushealth.com
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Custody exhibit — initial redlines and questions

Markus,

Thanks for sending the MSA + Order Form. Our legal team did an initial pass on the proposed custody/snapshot exhibit and we have a handful of open items that need alignment before we circulate for signature. High level:

- Scope: we need clearer language on which model artifacts are included in a "deployment snapshot" scope vs. operator-only artifacts.
- Redundancy / custody: request a clause that requires two geographically separated snapshot copies for disaster recovery if the deployment contains PHI.
- SLA carveouts: need explicit limitations for operator access windows, and a remediation credit proposal if evidence handover is delayed beyond agreed windows.
- Third-party attestation: we'd like a short attestation path (not full escrow) — periodic witness certification or notarized snapshot hash exchange.

Attached is a spreadsheet with line-item questions (Novus_Custody_Questions.xlsx). Can we get a redline that responds to the line items and a proposed timeline for evidence delivery?

We'd also like to schedule a 30-min call next week with security and your legal/ops leads to walk through the technical handoff and acceptance tests. Proposed times: Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Best,
Elena Torres
Senior Counsel, NovusHealth
elena.torres@novushealth.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custody exhibit — initial redlines and questions

Elena —

Appreciate the clear readout and the spreadsheet. I attached an initial working draft (redwood_custody_exhibit_v0.3.docx) that addresses each of your line items inline and includes two alternate clauses for operator-snapshot redundancy (Option A: geo-redundant copies for PHI; Option B: encrypted escrow with notarized hash).

Quick answers:
- Snapshot scope: we included a definition that excludes our model provenance tooling and internal training-data indices unless explicitly required in the Order Form.
- Redundancy: we can agree to geo-separated snapshots for PHI deployments; need to align on retention length and access controls.
- SLA credits: proposed 1% monthly service credit per full business day beyond the handover window, capped at 20% per quarter — open to negotiation.
- Attestation: we proposed a witness-certification path (quarterly attestation) as a lightweight alternative to escrow.

I looped in Marissa (deal owner) and David (legal for private deployments) to confirm commercial and legal appetite. Can you confirm availability for a 30-min call Wed 5/9 1:00pm PT?

Next steps: we can produce a single redlined exhibit for signature after the call, then feed the final exhibit into DocuSign. HubSpot record: HS-4821.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
phone: +1 415-555-0194

Attachment: redwood_custody_exhibit_v0.3.docx

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 May 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Custody exhibit — initial redlines and questions

Marissa / David — forwarding Novus thread and our draft. Key asks from Novus: geo-redundant snapshots for PHI, a defined evidence-handback window (they want 10 business days), and a light attestation (witness hash) in lieu of full escrow. Can we confirm:

- Commercial: is the customer-facing concession below acceptable? Novus has higher audit needs; I propose we offer a 6-month credit cap (instead of our default 3-month) if operator-level access is requested by their auditors. That gets them comfort without expanding liability.
- Legal: David, can you confirm whether Option B (encrypted escrow + notarized hash) creates any regulatory exposure we should avoid for this account? Also: retention ask of 3 years for PHI — do we push back?

David (inline):
> Markus — I read their spreadsheet. Suggested legal redlines are in the attached notes (see inline comments in the draft). High level responses:
> - We can accept geo-redundant snapshots for PHI with strict access gating (MFA + customer-signed w/ audit token). We should limit retention to 2 years by default and allow a one-time extension request tied to Order Form.
> - For the evidence-handback SLA, 10 business days is tight for high-volume snapshots; propose 15 business days for full forensic snapshots, 5 business days for lightweight hash-only deliveries.
> - Attestation: Witness-cert is fine, but for regulated PHI customers we should preserve the right to require a custodial escrow path triggered by specific incident thresholds.

Marissa (inline):
> Commercially, Novus is strategic in the east coast provider market — I recommend we take the 6-month credit cap concession in exchange for a single 12-month commitment on reserved capacity. That gives us predictability and is a reasonable trade.

If you both agree, I'll consolidate and respond to Elena with the proposed compromise and attach a redline for signature.

Thanks,
Markus

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 May 2028 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custody exhibit — initial redlines and questions

Elena —

Thanks again for the thorough pass. We're aligned on the core points and have a proposed compromise attached (Custody-SLA-Exhibit_Redlined_for_Novus.docx). Summary of the positions we've taken since your spreadsheet: 

1) Scope: snapshot definition now excludes model provenance and training indices unless explicitly listed in the Order Form; customer may request those artifacts but they will be defined in an exhibit schedule.
2) Redundancy: for PHI deployments we will maintain two geographically separated encrypted snapshot copies in independent custody, access gated by dual control + MFA. Retention default: 2 years; customer may request an extension in the Order Form (up to 3 years) with an additional fee.
3) Evidence-handback SLA: lightweight hash deliveries within 5 business days; full forensic snapshot deliveries within 15 business days. If we miss the agreed window, the customer receives a credit equal to 1% of monthly fees per elapsed full business day beyond the SLA, capped at 20% per quarter.
4) Attestation: we included a quarterly witness-certification option (lightweight) and preserved a triggered escrow path that Novus can request under defined incident thresholds.

Commercial concession: per Marissa's recommendation, Redwood is willing to increase the credit cap exposure to a 6-month aggregate cap in exchange for a 12-month reserved capacity commitment on the Order Form.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached redline and confirm whether the 12-month reserved capacity commitment is acceptable to Novus.
- If yes, we'll produce a final exhibit and route DocuSign (link: https://docusign.com/room/ABC-7382-sign).
- Technical handoff: propose Wed 5/16 10:00am PT for a 30-min runthrough with our ops lead (Lauren) and your CISO.

If you'd like, we can also add the notarized-hash escrow option as an optional appendix rather than the default path.

Best regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: Custody-SLA-Exhibit_Redlined_for_Novus.docx
